chapter: Wider talk: bands, places and players
title: Spanish Fort lakefront in summer
summary: He describes the open-air Tokyo Gardens at Spanish Fort and Tranchina's restaurant.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I just, when I compare a place like that with New Orleans, I wonder what it would be like to be on the lakefront, say, at the Spanish fort at, at Tokyo Gardens, in August. Uh, was it, how? It was wonderful. It was wonderful. It was cool, it was cool out, it was cool out there?
It was cool, you'd get the breeze off the, off the, off the, off the, off the, off the lake, see.
I mean, the, the place was an open, open air place.

Of course they had, uh, linoleum, uh, that they could roll up and down in case it was raining, and so it wouldn't mess up the dance floor, see, in case it was raining. Mm-hmm. Cause you know out there by the lake, it rains all the time in New Orleans.

So, it was, it was cool, and then Tranchini's had a, had a restaurant that was running late, later, later than, than we did, see, cause we used to get through at twelve o'clock, or something like that. Mm-hmm. And they had, uh, that was, uh, they had a big stage there, that, um, in case anybody wanted to, wanted to put some moving pictures on or something like that, they had a, had a, a stage, uh, and a, and a screen for, for the movies or something like that, you know.
What about, uh, have any mosquitoes out there?
Well, I don't know, mosquitoes in New Orleans. Yeah. Always got mosquitoes there, you know. Yeah. I mean, they're out there in the swamps, you know. Better than it used to be.
